summary.one_liner: A long-form, opinionated guide to the principles, pipeline stages, serving concerns, evaluation practices, and tools involved in building search systems.
summary.what_it_does: This is a written guide rather than software: it walks through the search problem, starting with questions to pin down corpus size, media, latency, access control, and multilingual needs. It then covers the search pipeline stages: index selection, spam and duplicate filtering, inverted index construction, query analysis and expansion, and ranking including learning to rank. It also discusses serving concerns such as latency, caching, and sharding, and how to measure quality with metrics like precision, recall, MAP, and nDCG, plus human evaluation and golden sets. A final section lists SaaS options, open source libraries (Lucene, Solr, Elasticsearch, Xapian, Sphinx, Whoosh, Lunr and others), public datasets, and reference books.
use_cases: Planning a search feature for a product
Learning how search engines are structured
Choosing between hosted search services and open source engines
Finding public datasets for building a search prototype
Picking a search library for embedded or client-side use
notable: Organizes search knowledge as a pipeline (index selection, index construction, query analysis, ranking, serving) and explains how changes upstream ripple downstream
Emphasizes evaluation processes, golden sets, and human raters as the hardest part of search work
Uses a legend of icons to flag SaaS, open source, language bindings, gotchas, and notable ideas
Includes a curated set of tools by language (JavaScript, Python, Java, C/C++) and a list of public datasets such as Common Crawl and OpenStreetMap dumps
caveats: Not a tutorial or complete reference; the author states it is a starting map that may miss important topics
Some sections are thin or unfinished, such as the spam and index selection subsections that end abruptly
Tool and SaaS information reflects the time of writing and may be outdated
